speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To understand the underlying cause, have you noticed any abdominal pain, bloating, or changes in your bowel or bladder habits recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Cancer with Malignant Ascites.

The clinical picture of a large ovarian mass, significant abdominal girth increase (ascites), and shortness of breath in a 40-year-old woman is highly suggestive of advanced ovarian malignancy. Given the severity of the symptoms and the physical findings, immediate diagnostic workup is required. I will now request a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to assess the extent of the disease and confirm the presence of ascites and metastasis.

REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen_Pelvis
